backup.section.title: Notebox backup
backup.section.intro: Periodically creates a zip archive (with optional encryption) of the currently in-use notebox to a destination of your choice. Backups run while the app is open. You can create ad-hoc backups, manually from the command palette ({modifier} + P → “Back up notebox now”).
backup.enabled.label: Notebox backup & restore
backup.enabled.description: When off, scheduled backups don't run and the manual command is disabled. Your destination folder and other settings are retained. Turn on to enable backups or restore files from a backup.
backup.destination.label: Destination folder
backup.destination.description: Where archives are written. If empty, backups will be disabled.
backup.destination.cannotUseNotebox: Cannot use the notebox folder (or a subfolder of it) as a backup destination — backups would archive themselves.
backup.interval.label: Backup interval (hours)
backup.interval.description: How often to back up while the app is running. 0 disables scheduled backups (manual runs still work).
backup.keepCount.label: Retain this many backups
backup.keepCount.description: Older archives matching the filename pattern are pruned after each successful backup.
backup.onlyOnChange.label: Only back up when something changed
backup.onlyOnChange.description: Skip the scheduled backup if no notebox file has been modified since the last successful run. Manual runs always proceed.
backup.includeUserConfig.label: Include user settings folder
backup.includeUserConfig.description: Bundle your global InkyCap settings (theme, fonts, creation rules, bookmarks) alongside the notebox. Useful when restoring on a new machine.
backup.filenamePattern.label: Filename pattern
backup.filenamePattern.description: Template for each archive. Tokens: {tokens}. Reserved characters are replaced with _.
backup.password.label: Password protection (optional)
backup.password.description: When set, archives will be encrypted with AES-256. InkyCap will attempt to store the password in your OS keychain. It will not write it in the settings file or elsewhere. Keep track of it.
backup.password.perArchiveNotice: The password is bound to each archive at the moment it is created. Changing or clearing the password here affects only the next backup. Existing archives keep the password they were made with so you must use that particular password to restore them.
backup.password.unrecoverableWarning: ⚠ If you lose this password, the backup becomes unrecoverable. There is no reset.
backup.password.saved: Password saved to OS keychain. Future backups will use this password; existing archives keep their original password.
backup.password.cleared: Password cleared. Future backups will be unencrypted. Existing encrypted archives still need their original password to restore.
backup.password.confirmChangeBody: This new password will be used for future backups only. Existing archives remain encrypted with the password they were made with, and you'll need that particular password to restore them. Continue?
backup.password.confirmClearBody: Future backups will no longer be encrypted. Existing encrypted archives still need their original password to restore. Clearing the keychain does not unlock them. Continue?
backup.lastBackup.label: Last backup
backup.runNow.paletteHint: Or trigger from the command palette ({modifier} + P → “Back up notebox now”).
backup.toast.skipped: Backup skipped (no changes since last run).
backup.browse.title: Browse backups
backup.browse.intro: Choose a backup archive to restore your entire notebox or selected files.
backup.browse.noArchives: No backup archives found in the destination folder yet.
backup.browse.targetOriginalDisabled: Open a notebox to restore in place
backup.browse.passwordHint: Each archive is encrypted with the password that was active when it was created. The current password from the OS keychain is used by default; type a different password here only if this archive was made with one. Leave empty to use the keychain.
backup.browse.noPassword: This archive is encrypted. No password is set in the OS keychain — type the password the archive was created with before restoring.
git.toolbar.title: Collaboration (Git)
git.panel.title: Collaboration via Git
git.setup.intro: Synchronize this notebox using Git to collaborate or for your convenience on different computers. Sync merges collaborators' changes automatically; conflicts will appear as inline suggestions for you to resolve and all changes will be displayed along with a history to revert to, if desired.
git.setup.tokenHint: Stored in your operating system's keychain, never in the notebox. Leave blank to use a secure sign-in (ssh-agent or your default key).
git.setup.identityHint: Shown as the author on your changes so collaborators can see who made each edit. Pre-filled from your Git identity (if you have one set). Change it to use a different name for this notebox.
git.setup.repairHint: This notebox is set up for collaboration, but there is no local git repository behind it (the .git folder is missing, or the notebox hasn't been cloned from a remote repository on to this computer). Re-initialize it below to reconnect — your remote and branch are pre-filled.
git.setup.offlineHint: Collaborate with no git server: share this notebox by exporting it — with its full history — to a single file, and reconcile changes by importing files others send back. Choose this when you have no hosted git remote. You can add a remote later.
git.reconnect.intro: This notebox is already linked to a remote ({remote}, branch {branch}) but isn't set up for collaboration here. Reconnect to pick up where you left off.
git.review.toggleHint: When on, a Sync or package import pauses and shows every incoming change as a suggestion to accept or reject, instead of merging automatically. Your own edits are never dropped — accepting takes a collaborator's change on top of yours. Applies to both Git-server sync and package handoff. A per-device setting; it doesn't affect collaborators.
git.review.toggleFailed: Could not change the review setting
git.bundle.toggleHint: When on, sharing this notebox (Sync push or package export) first copies the Typst packages it uses — and their dependencies — into the notebox, so collaborators can compile without downloading anything. Off by default: published @preview packages download automatically on each person's side. Turn this on for @local packages (which can't be downloaded) or offline sharing. A per-device setting; turning it on bundles the current packages right away.
git.bundle.toggleFailed: Could not change the package-bundling setting
git.review.heading: Review incoming changes
git.review.intro: Open each note and accept or reject its incoming changes in the Changes panel on the right. Your notebox stays on its current content until you Accept reviewed & finish below — that step merges every reviewed note and brings your notebox up to date.
git.conflict.heading: Conflicts to resolve
git.conflict.intro: These notes were edited on both sides. Open each one and resolve its suggestions in the Changes panel on the right. Your notebox stays on its current content until you finalize below — that step merges every resolved note and brings your notebox up to date.
git.settings.heading: Notebox settings changed on both sides
git.settings.intro: Edits to different settings were merged automatically. Pick a value for each setting you both changed:
git.discard.title: Discard merge
git.discard.confirm: Discard this merge and restore the notebox to its last committed state? The incoming changes stay on the remote — you can Sync again later. Any unsaved in-progress resolution is lost.
git.manage.heading: Manage collaboration
git.manage.tokenPlaceholder: Leave blank to keep your current token
git.manage.disableConfirm: Stop collaborating on this notebox? The git repository and your files stay on disk; only InkyCap's collaboration link is removed.

git.package.passwordHint: Leave blank for no encryption. If set, the package is AES-256 encrypted — share the password with collaborators separately (it is never stored). The same password is used to import an encrypted package.

mycelial.help.title: The Mycelial View
mycelial.help.heading.grow: Where Does Your Knowledge Want to Grow?
mycelial.help.lead: This view helps you identify what you have not yet written in your notebox. Mycelial View is computed around the note you opened it from (the anchor) but it is not a graphical map of existing links.
mycelial.help.anchorBody: the note this view is built around. Everything else is found relative to it.
mycelial.help.sourceBody: other existing notes that contribute to the signal. Click one to rebuild the view around it.
mycelial.help.latentBodyBefore: an existing page that other notes mention by name without linking to it. Click it to see those mentions, then open one to add the wikilink
mycelial.help.emergentBody: a phrase that recurs across several notes but has no page yet. Click it to create that page (a long phrase will prompt you to trim its title first).
mycelial.help.pathsBody: A path (connective line) means two nodes share a signal. Thicker paths are stronger signals; faint grey paths are ordinary wikilinks between notes. Hovering a node highlights just its paths.
mycelial.help.whyBody: InkyCap looks at the anchor note plus its neighbourhood (notes it links to and the notes that read as most similar to it) and finds words or short phrases that recur in that neighbourhood in a distinctive way. If a recurring phrase matches an existing page, it surfaces as a latent link; if it has no page, it surfaces as an emergent concept. That's why a concept can appear even though you never wrote it as a heading—it was repeated often enough to stand out.
mycelial.help.legendBody: click a type to hide or show it.
mycelial.help.depthBody: how many wikilink hops out to scan.
mycelial.help.conceptFilteringBody: (right panel): see which words were held back from concept detection, rescue ones that matter, and add your own words to ignore.
mycelialFilter.empty: Nothing was filtered out of this note's neighbourhood. Words shown here recur enough to be concepts but were held back as stopwords.
mycelialFilter.rescueUserTitle: Remove from your stopword list so this can surface as a concept
mycelialFilter.rescueBuiltinTitle: Treat as a concept — adds it to the notebox dictionary so it's no longer filtered
